Now I have enough context. Let me implement the bootstrap and demo shelf changes.
Unit tests pass. Now let's build and run the required Playwright first-run journey.
The new first-run seed correctly makes every fresh browser context show the demo, which breaks the pre-existing journeys that assume an empty shelf. I'll isolate them from first-run state while keeping the demo journey genuinely fresh.
## Result — DEMO-3: First-run seeding, demo removal, and contextual hints

### What was implemented

- **`src/app/AppBootstrap.tsx`** — checks the demo flag/case count via the existing one-time seeder before routes mount. Normal seeding completes before the shelf's case read; failures and a 5-second grace timeout still open the app. The seed promise is shared across StrictMode effect replay, so a fresh install seeds once. Production loading is dynamic, keeping demo images and the image pipeline out of the initial shell chunk.
- **`src/App.tsx`** — mounts `AppBootstrap` inside `AppShell` around the route table, with an injectable first-run seed for tests.
- **`src/features/shelf/CaseCard.tsx` / `CaseShelf.tsx` / `CaseShelfPage.tsx` / `DeleteCaseDialog.tsx` / `shelf.css`** — added the `Demo` ribbon, the `Demo case — remove it whenever you like.` copy, demo-first shelf ordering, `Remove demo` wording, demo-named confirmation copy, and removal through `removeDemoCase` so the install flag is re-asserted and user cases are untouched.
- **`src/features/case/CaseBoardPage.tsx`** — thread-anchor hint at two or more cards; long-press hint when `(pointer: coarse)` and a card is selected; each dismiss marks the hint seen through the existing store.
- **`src/features/recall/RecallPage.tsx`** — recall hint only after the first real connection exists.
- **`src/features/onboarding/hints.css`** — contextual hints are click-through except their actions, so they never block board pointer work.
- **`tests/demo/firstRun.test.tsx`** — bootstrap seeding, existing-case skip, failure/timeout fallback, demo ribbon/removal isolation, thread-anchor/long-press/recall trigger tests.
- **`e2e/demo.spec.ts`** — fresh-context first-run journey: seed → open → graph/readiness → hint dismissal → demo removal → reload empty shelf → Settings replay.
- **`e2e/fixtures/no-demo-storage.json` + `playwright.config.ts`** — isolates unrelated existing journeys from the first-run demo and one-time hints; `demo.spec.ts` explicitly overrides with empty storage state.
- **`tests/pwa/UpdatePrompt.test.tsx` / `tests/recall/RecallPage.test.tsx`** — narrowed update-prompt assertions past the new bootstrap live region, and raised the lazy-board lookup timeout for full-suite stability.

### Acceptance evidence

| Criterion | Evidence | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh install seeds exactly one labeled demo before shelf renders | Bootstrap test with real `seedDemoCase`; demo e2e asserts one `isDemo` case, 6 cards, 5 connections | Pass |
| Existing case seeds nothing and sets flag | Bootstrap test with a pre-existing case; flag set, no demo row | Pass |
| Demo removal confirmed, user cases untouched, no reseed on reload | Component test with demo + user case; e2e removal, zero demo rows, reload empty shelf | Pass |
| Hints trigger once at their moment and replay from Settings | Component tests for all three triggers; e2e dismissal + Settings replay with focus return | Pass |
| Playwright first-run journey | 3/3 projects passed: desktop 1440×900, tablet 1280×800, phone 390×844 | Pass |

### Accessibility

- Hint opening moves focus to the non-modal panel; `Got it`/Escape restore focus to the board/recall heading, Settings restores the replay trigger.
- Demo removal confirmation keeps Cancel as initial focus, closes on Escape, and restores focus via the shared Dialog.
- New actions use `Button`/existing 44px targets; no new control is below 44×44.
- All new CSS uses semantic tokens only; no raw palette values. No new animation; existing reduced-motion rule removes hint entrance motion.
- No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; all demo/title copy is plain text.

### Validation run

- `npm test -- tests/demo/firstRun.test.tsx` — **13 passed**
- `npm run test:e2e -- e2e/demo.spec.ts` — **3 passed** (desktop, tablet, phone)
- `npm test` — **79 files, 988 tests passed**
- `npm run typecheck` — passed
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors (3 pre-existing `RecallSummary.tsx` warnings)
- `npm run format:check` — passed

### Shared files / handoff

- `playwright.config.ts` now applies `e2e/fixtures/no-demo-storage.json` to every project. The file sets the demo seed flag and all three hints seen. `e2e/demo.spec.ts` overrides this to a genuinely fresh context. Preserve that override when adding any new first-run journey.
- `CaseShelfPage` now routes demo deletion through `removeDemoCase` and accepts an optional `demoFlagStore`. Preserve the `isDemo` guard: user cases must never use the demo removal path.
- `CaseBoardPage.hintStore` and `RecallPage.hintStore` are injectable for tests; defaults remain the install-level `hintSeenStore`.

### Known gaps

- Long-press is verified with a mocked coarse-pointer `matchMedia` in jsdom; Playwright projects use desktop Chrome without touch emulation, so there is no browser-level coarse-pointer journey.
- Contextual hints are fixed near the viewport bottom rather than geometrically anchored to a specific card/control. They are click-through except for actions; placement is worth including in the human style review.
- Pre-existing full-suite E2E failures in `board.spec.ts` (pan/fallback link) and `connections.spec.ts` (type menu) reproduce on a clean HEAD worktree and are unrelated to DEMO-3.

handoff.summary: Implemented DEMO-3: AppBootstrap seeds the demo once before routes mount with a failure/timeout fallback, the shelf labels and removes only the demo, thread-anchor/long-press/recall hints are contextually wired and replayable, and the fresh-context Playwright journey passes on desktop, tablet, and phone. Required unit and browser checks, full unit suite, typecheck, lint, and formatting pass.
decisions: Bootstrap waits for the normal seed so the shelf's single case read includes the demo, but a 5-second grace timeout and swallowed seed failures ensure the shelf is never permanently blocked.

Only one board hint is shown at a time: thread-anchor at two or more cards, then long-press only on a coarse pointer with a selected card. The recall hint lives on the recall screen and requires at least one real connection.
Demo deletion uses removeDemoCase so the install-level seed flag is re-asserted; ordinary user cases still use the normal delete path.
Unrelated Playwright journeys use a storage fixture that pre-sets the demo flag and seen hints, while demo.spec.ts overrides it with empty storage to exercise first-run behavior.
Contextual hint panels are click-through except their actions so they never block board pointer work.
tests: npm run test:e2e -- e2e/demo.spec.ts: 3 passed (desktop, tablet-landscape, phone)
npm run lint: 0 errors (3 pre-existing warnings)
warnings: The full E2E suite still has pre-existing failures in board.spec.ts and connections.spec.ts; both reproduce on a clean HEAD worktree and are unrelated to DEMO-3.
Blocked localStorage still means the demo seed flag cannot survive a reload; this limitation is inherited from the existing seed store.
validationLimitations: Long-press hint behavior is component-tested with a mocked coarse-pointer matchMedia; Playwright's configured projects do not emulate touch, so the browser journey exercises the thread-anchor hint instead.

Contextual hints are fixed near the viewport bottom rather than geometrically anchored to their trigger; their click-through body avoids blocking the board, but final placement is a human style-review matter.
